title: A Salt for the Choir Anew
premise: Emrys Nystrom, a hedge-witch's runaway apprentice turned charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Greyharrow, is handed a dying stranger's map to the Court Beneath the Mountain — where his old mistress sold her own soul twenty years ago to buy the city's amnesty, and now serves as a hollow-eyed thrall of the Winter King. Pursued by the Magistrate's witch-hunters and shadowed by the stranger's vengeful daughter, Emrys descends through the mountain's bone-roads, discovering that the court's power runs on inherited debts: every soul sold there can be reclaimed only by someone who willingly takes on the seller's bargain. At the winter solstice, Emrys chooses to assume his mistress's debt himself, unmaking the Winter King's claim on the city but binding his own soul to the court — until the daughter, Sef, pays the final price in his stead, breaking the cycle of inheritance. The long winter breaks; Emrys returns to Greyharrow carrying magic openly for the first time, justice delivered outside any law.
about_author: Vesper Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives early and stays late.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In outlawed-magic Greyharrow, Emrys sells luck-knots and fever-charms from a market stall, hiding his craft behind mundane trinkets. A raid by the Magistrate's hunters nearly catches him; he escapes but loses his stock and his nerve. Emotional beat: weary survival, the cost of a life spent small and hidden.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A frostbitten stranger collapses against Emrys's tenement door, pressing a wax-sealed map into his hands and gasping a name: Maren Nystrom, Emrys's old mistress. The man dies whispering that the debt comes due at solstice. Emotional beat: dread awakening; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The map shows roads beneath the mountain but blanks itself wherever the court lies. Emrys deciphers his mistress's handwriting in the margins and learns she sold her soul to purchase the city's amnesty — the law that outlawed magic was her price paid in flesh. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Captain Ilsa Vane. Witch-hunter Vane finds the dead stranger and traces the map's seal to Emrys's district, opening a ledger page that has waited twenty years. She suspects the runaway apprentice still lives. Emotional beat: cold, methodical purpose; justice as paperwork and iron.

chapters.title: Sef
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The dead stranger's daughter, Sef, tracks Emrys intending to kill him for stealing her father's map — then relents when he shows her the truth of the soul-debt. Her father died trying to reclaim her mother's sold soul alone. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Fleeing Vane's raid on the market quarter, Emrys and Sef enter the mountain through a collapsed mine, following bone-roads lit by lichen that feeds on memory. Each mile costs them a recollection. Emotional beat: wonder soured by loss; descent as erasure.

chapters.title: Tolls and Tollmen
chapters.summary: POV Sef. A tollman of the court demands payment in names. Sef bargains away her father's name to pass, and feels him fading from her memory even as they walk. Emrys realizes the mountain eats inheritance itself. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. They find the sold souls: a choir of the hollow, singing the Winter King's endless mass. Among them, a face Emrys knows — his mistress Maren, eyes like frosted glass, singing without self. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Maren (flashback chapters interleaved). Through the choir's resonance, Maren's memories surface: the plague winter, the Magistrate's ultimatum, her choice to sell herself so hedge-witches might live. Emotional beat: tragic nobility reframed as an unforgivable abandonment.

chapters.title: Vane Descends
chapters.summary: POV Captain Vane. Following Emrys's trail, Vane enters the mountain with a warrant and a squad — and discovers the court has been buying souls from Greyharrow's own magistrates for generations. Her certainty cracks. Emotional beat: faith in law beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Bargain-Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The court's steward explains the rule: a soul may be reclaimed only if another willingly assumes the seller's debt entire — term, service, and silence. Emrys understands what the dying stranger attempted, and failed. Emotional beat: the trap's elegant cruelty laid bare.

chapters.title: What Sef Carries
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Sef confesses her mother sold her own soul to shield Sef from a blood-debt of their family's making; her father's quest was penance. She means to assume the debt herself and end her line's chain. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Above, Greyharrow's first true snow in decades begins — the Winter King extending his season as solstice nears, hungry for new signatures. Refugees choke the roads. Emotional beat: mounting dread; time running out like sand.

chapters.title: Interlude in Iron
chapters.summary: POV Captain Vane. Captured by the court's tollmen, Vane is offered freedom in exchange for signing over her dead brother's soul, held in escrow since his execution. She refuses — the first refusal the court has heard in a century. Emotional beat: defiance kindled in a broken believer.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys sings counterpoint to the choir using his mistress's teaching, and Maren flickers — one bar of selfhood, enough to warn him: the King reads intentions, so carry none. Emotional beat: tenderness inside danger; love as tradecraft.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The court gathers for the renewal of contracts. Sef moves to sign her mother's debt; Emrys, carrying no intention, signs Maren's first — outmaneuvering both Sef and the King. Emotional beat: quiet audacity; the apprentice surpassing every teacher.

chapters.title: The Debt Assumed
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The debt floods in: twenty years of servitude, the King's voice in his skull, Maren freed and collapsing. He feels the choir's pull begin to take him. Emotional beat: terrible cost accepted with open eyes.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of the Winter King
chapters.summary: POV multiple, braided. Inside the debt, Emrys finds its flaw: the King's power is itself inherited, a stolen crown passed hand to hand for a thousand years. Emrys refuses to inherit it — and Sef, arriving through the choir, declares the whole ledger void by paying with her line's original blood-debt. The King unravels. Emotional beat: climax; the cycle broken not by power but by refusal.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Snowlight
chapters.summary: POV Captain Vane. The mountain exhales; the sold souls wake or dissolve into peace. Vane, warrant in ash, must choose between arresting Emrys and burning her ledger. She burns it. Emotional beat: grace; justice choosing itself over law.

chapters.title: Maren's Farewell
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Freed but mortal and frail, Maren walks Emrys to the mountain's mouth, gives him back the lessons he fled, and asks nothing. She stays to help rebuild the court as a refuge rather than a prison. Emotional beat: forgiveness given and received, without absolution being cheap.

chapters.title: Open Signs
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Spring reaches Greyharrow. Emrys reopens his stall with charms labeled honestly, magic no longer contraband, while Sef — her debt discharged, her name half-restored — stands beside him as partner. Vane watches from across the square and does not intervene. Emotional beat: cautious hope; a life no longer hidden.

chapters.title: A Salt for the Choir Anew
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. On the first anniversary of the breaking, Emrys carries salt to the mountain's threshold for the choir's remembrance rite, honoring those who woke and those who didn't. He writes his own name in the ledger's margin — freely given, freely kept. Emotional beat: closure; inheritance transformed from burden into gift.
